analysis: After ventricular systole, the volume of blood in the ventricle is the end-diastolic volume. This is because during systole, the ventricle contracts, leading to a decrease in blood volume, which then reaches its lowest point before the next diastole. The end-diastolic volume represents the amount of blood in the ventricle at the end of diastole, just before the next contraction.
